purpose: Test whether the negative body-size gradient in adjusted species wet-recruitment responses persists within taxonomic families rather than arising only from between-family differences.

method.complete_cases: 26 species with adjusted response and positive finite Body_size_mm
method.y: adjusted per-species wet-vs-dry intercept log odds
method.residualization: Subtract weighted family mean from x and y within each family represented by >=2 complete species. Singleton families contribute zero within-family variation and are excluded from the slope denominator.
method.permutation: Permute x values among species within each family, preserving family membership, y, and weights.
method.directional_summary: also report fraction Tperm <= Tobs because discovery sign is negative

family_specific.rule: For each family with >=5 complete species, report weighted simple slope of adjusted response on log body size; descriptive only.

interpretation.significant_negative_within_family: Supports a body-size gradient not reducible to broad between-family differences.
interpretation.null: Body-size result may largely reflect family-level ecological differences and should not be a headline mechanism.
boundaries: Body size remains a proxy for hydric/life-history traits.
